verdict.rationale: The Reader GitHub docs document an `x-wait-for-selector` header that makes the API wait for a specific element before returning, shown with a curl example. A headless-Chrome `browser` engine (`x-engine`) and `x-respond-timing` controls support JS-rendered pages. The community question about dynamic JS support is open skepticism, not a concrete contradiction. missing for 10: detailed documentation of wait semantics (timeouts, failure behavior when the selector never appears, multiple selectors), independent or hands-on corroboration that the selector wait works.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the API wait for a specific selector to appear before returning the rendered page

citations.quote:
wait for a specific element
curl 'https://r.jina.ai/https://example.com/' -H 'x-wait-for-selector: #content'
`x-engine` — enforces a fetching engine: `browser` (headless Chrome), `curl` (lightweight, no JS), or `auto`
`x-respond-timing` — explicit control over *when* Reader is willing to return.
